# How chorus builds the vendored libopus 1.6.1: the one list the endpoint's host
# build (firmware/Makefile), the Rust client's sys crate (crates/opus-sys/build.rs)
# and the ESP-IDF image read, so the three compile the same code the same way.
#
# `define NAME` is a preprocessor definition; `source path` a translation unit
# relative to this directory. The set is the decoder and nothing else: it was
# found by linking opus_decoder_create, opus_decode, opus_decode24 and
# OPUS_GET_FINAL_RANGE against libopus's own source lists (opus_sources.mk,
# celt_sources.mk, silk_sources.mk in the release archive) minus every encoder
# unit, and adding back what the linker named. src/opus_compare.c is vendored
# beside it as the conformance tool (not a library unit).
#
# FIXED_POINT: the fixed-point decoder, chosen for the ESP32-S3 and kept on the
#   host so the host's decode IS the endpoint's (third_party/README.md says why).
# ENABLE_RES24: 24-bit internal resolution for fixed point, libopus 1.6's own
#   default (configure.ac, --disable-fixed-res24 turns it off); opus_decode24
#   then returns the decoder's full resolution.
# DISABLE_FLOAT_API: no float entry points, so nothing in the decoder uses float.
# VAR_ARRAYS: scratch on the stack as C99 variable-length arrays (libopus's
#   stack_alloc.h), no pseudostack and no alloca.
define OPUS_BUILD
define FIXED_POINT
define ENABLE_RES24
define DISABLE_FLOAT_API
define VAR_ARRAYS
